figures.title: Rival predictions and deciding observations
figures.caption: These are project-authored prospective tests. The strongest supported reading is selective continuity: inherited outlines and alignment coexist with local rebuilding and changed access. rivals.name: Shared coordination
rivals.prediction: Through-routes survive rebuilding more often than internal divisions; connected repairs share independent dates.
rivals.challenge: A complete, powered matched study shows no predicted route advantage, or repair timing follows only engineering and distance.

rivals.name: Engineering constraints
rivals.prediction: Durable foundations, grade and drainage explain retention; effects weaken after material and preservation controls.
rivals.challenge: The route advantage persists within the same foundations, materials and exposure, while network relationships predict repair better.

rivals.name: Inherited parcel rights
rivals.prediction: Frontage and parcel boundaries persist while internal rooms and household access change.
rivals.challenge: Boundaries reset freely while shared connections persist across the resets, with no parcel continuity needed.

rivals.name: Local infill and maintenance
rivals.prediction: Small additions narrow or close access at different times; service replacement follows clogging and local need.
rivals.challenge: Independently dated coordinated repairs and repeated open-network preservation exceed the local engineering model.
